Threshold positions across recovery — the ceiling has come back

VT1 = VE/VO₂ nadir wattage (aerobic threshold). VT2 = VE/VCO₂ nadir wattage (respiratory compensation point / sustainable-work ceiling).

195 → 197 → 224 W Dec → Day-4 → Day-8. VT1 has shifted RIGHT on Day-8 (+28 W vs Dec). Nadir value also deeper (18.32 vs 18.59). Aerobic threshold appears improved — possibly transient (plasma volume effect).
269 → 229 → 269 W VT2 has fully recovered. Dropped 40 W on Day-4 (229 W), back to Dec baseline (269 W) by Day-8. Sustainable-work ceiling restored.
▼ Interpretation — VT1 & VT2 recovery trajectory — ceiling restored AND aerobic threshold improved VT1: 195→224 W (+28) • VT2: 229→269 W (recovered)

Two big findings on Day-8 from the nadir analysis:

(1) VT2 has fully recovered. The Day-4 leftward shift (40 W drop to 229 W) has reversed completely. Day-8 nadir is at 269 W — Dec baseline (269 W) restored. Sustainable-work ceiling is back. Note also the entire VE/VCO₂ curve sits much lower than Dec on Day-8 (20-23 vs 24-27): Dylan is moving less air per unit CO₂ cleared at every wattage, which means more efficient gas exchange overall.

(2) VT1 has actually shifted RIGHT and DEEPER. Dec nadir was at 195 W (value 18.59). Day-8 nadir is at 224 W (value 18.32) — both farther right (more wattage tolerated at the aerobic threshold) AND lower in absolute VE/VO₂ (more efficient O₂ extraction). This is a meaningful aerobic improvement that wasn't there on Day-4 (when carb-driven CO₂ load was pushing the curve up).

Interpretation: some of the Day-8 advantages are likely transient — plasma volume expansion is masking the underlying state by lowering ventilatory demand at any given workload. As PV normalizes (1-3 weeks) the curves may drift back up. Worth watching whether VT1/VT2 values stabilize at the Day-8 position or relax back to Dec by Day-12 or Day-16.

Practical implication: the physiological ceiling is back AND there's an apparent aerobic efficiency bonus. Threshold and tempo work is mechanically safe again. The substrate machinery (see below) is the slower-recovering piece — Z2/endurance pacing should still be gentle until fat-ox normalizes.

Lactate — Day-4 vs Day-8, with step-to-step dynamics

Capillary samples taken at end of each step (no sample at 125 W on Day-8; first sample at 150 W). Δ and rates computed from time elapsed between consecutive samples (which includes any rest gaps between steps). No fixed thresholds shown — per-step dynamics are the diagnostic.

Lactate response curve — Day-4 vs Day-8

▼ Interpretation — Lactate at top steps has dropped substantially — confirms VT2 recovery 250 W: Day-4 1.6 → Day-8 0.8 mmol/L

This is the most powerful single piece of evidence for VT2 recovery — and it comes from a completely independent measurement system (capillary blood vs ventilatory gas). At the same 250 W wattage:

  • Day-4: 1.6 mmol/L — already producing meaningful anaerobic contribution
  • Day-8: 0.8 mmol/L — half of Day-4. Solidly aerobic.

225 W tells the same story: Day-4 1.0 → Day-8 0.7. The crossover toward anaerobic contribution that was happening at 225 W on Day-4 simply isn't happening at 225 W on Day-8.

The 150 W reading (0.9 on Day-8 vs 0.4 on Day-4) is the well-known warm-up washout artifact. By 175 W it has cleared (Day-8 drops to 0.5, identical to Day-4). Don't read anything into the warm-up wattage difference — it reflects residual lactate from pre-test activity, not steady-state physiology.

Post-test peak of 1.8 mmol/L (sampled 2-5 min after stopping) tells us Dylan ended the 275 W step with meaningful lactate still in muscle that was still washing into blood — normal post-effort dynamics. Even this peak is well below what a Day-4 max test would have produced.

Featured chart. Same as the original Day-4 comparison but now extended with Day-8. Watch how the deep-breath pattern at top steps has settled.

▼ Interpretation — Day-8 breath pattern has dropped back below Dec — substrate-driven TV/FEV1 at 250 W: 50 → 68 → 60%

Day-8 TV/FEV1 sits between Dec and Day-4. The deep-slow pattern Dylan showed on Day-4 (68% at top step) has partially relaxed back. At 250 W: Dec 50% → Day-4 68% → Day-8 60%.

This supports the "downstream of CO₂ load" interpretation from the Day-4 report: as carb-burning has come down (lower CHO ox and RER), CO₂ production has come down, and ventilation demand has eased — so deep breathing isn't as necessary. The breath pattern is following the substrate, not the other way around.

If you wanted breath-pattern improvement to "stick" independent of metabolic state, the way to get that would be deliberate breath work and high-VE intervals. Doesn't seem to happen passively as a recovery side-effect.

Muscle oxygen — Day-8 NIRS data (first time available)

Quad (working muscle) and bicep (non-working muscle) SmO₂ trends per step. Linear regression slope computed over each step skipping the first 90s (Chay convention). Positive slope = re-oxygenating; negative slope = desaturating (demand > supply). No NIRS data exists for Dec or Day-4 so Day-8 is the new baseline for this metric.

Mean SmO₂ per step — quad vs bicep

▼ Interpretation — Quad desaturates progressively, bicep buffers — classic working/non-working pattern quad 58% → 30% • bicep 71% → 57%

Quad (working muscle) desaturates steadily across the test from 58% at 125 W to 30% at 275 W. That's a 28-point drop, with the steepest single-step drop at the 200 W step (49→41 over the step) — meaningful demand-supply imbalance there.

Bicep (non-working muscle) is doing its job as O₂ reservoir. Stays in the 55-71% range and shows reoxygenation between steps. The bicep's "rebound" at 250 W (+3.0%/min slope) is the non-working muscle re-oxygenating during a sustained plateau — classic cycling pattern.

This is the new NIRS baseline. Future tests can compare directly. The interesting follow-up: does quad SmO₂ at matched watts come UP as recovery progresses (better O₂ delivery) or stay where it is (no recovery effect on O₂ kinetics)?

Your notes / comments on this metric

Quad SmO₂ trend per step (slopes)

Each segment shows start→end SmO₂ within the regression window (first 90s of each step skipped). Tilt = slope direction. Green = re-oxygenating; red = desaturating. Slope shown in %/min.

▼ Interpretation — Quad slope analysis — major desat at 200 W and 275 W 200 W: −2.4%/min • 275 W: −3.8%/min

Two negative-slope steps stand out: 200 W (−2.4%/min) and 275 W (−3.8%/min). These are the wattages where quad O₂ demand most clearly exceeds supply during the step.

200 W is interesting: it's at VT1, the wattage where the aerobic system should be most efficient. The fact that quad SmO₂ desaturates strongly there suggests Dylan's quad is working closer to its O₂-extraction limit at moderate watts than the metabolic markers alone would suggest. Possibly recovery-state related — the muscle is meeting demand by extracting more O₂ from a slightly compromised supply.

275 W is the test ceiling: quad collapsing here is expected — we're approaching/at VT2 (269 W).

225-250 W shows quad nearly flat slopes (-0.2, +0.8 %/min): at these watts the quad has stabilized at a low SmO₂ (~36-42%) and is in steady-state extraction. Useful — confirms VT1 to VT2 range is the sustainable extraction zone.

Your notes / comments on this metric

Bicep SmO₂ trend per step (slopes)

▼ Interpretation — Bicep pattern — non-working muscle as O₂ buffer positive rebound at 200 W and 250 W

Bicep slopes flip direction across the test in a meaningful pattern. Slight desat through 150-225 W as overall O₂ demand rises, then a strong re-ox spike at 250 W (+3.0%/min) as the bicep "gives" its O₂ reserve to working muscles during sustained moderate effort, then desat again at 275 W.

The 250 W bicep rebound is the most interesting signature. Non-working muscle re-oxygenating during a hard plateau suggests Dylan's circulatory system is redistributing blood flow effectively — pulling O₂ from non-working tissue and sending it to the quads. That's a sign of good circulatory adaptation.

275 W desat (-1.6%/min): at the test ceiling, even the bicep's O₂ reserve is being drawn down — the whole system is working hard.

Day-8 summary — where Dylan sits in his recovery curve

THE CEILING IS BACK — AND THE FLOOR HAS LIFTED

VT2 has fully recovered from its Day-4 left-shift. Dec baseline was 269 W; Day-4 dropped to 229 W; Day-8 is back at 269 W. The entire VE/VCO₂ curve also sits noticeably lower than Dec at every wattage — more efficient breathing per unit CO₂.

VT1 has shifted right. Dec nadir at 195 W; Day-8 nadir at 224 W with a deeper value. Aerobic threshold appears to have improved by ~30 W. Some of this may be transient (plasma volume lowering VE at any given workload), but the magnitude is notable.

Lactate independently confirms VT2 recovery. At 250 W: Day-4 was 1.6 mmol/L, Day-8 is 0.8 mmol/L — half. At 225 W: 1.0 → 0.7. Two independent measurement systems (ventilatory gas and capillary blood) agree on the same picture: anaerobic contribution at top steps has dropped substantially.

SUBSTRATE — PARTIAL RECOVERY

CHO and RER have walked back from Day-4 peak toward Dec at top steps. Fat ox has only partially recovered. The substrate machinery is on a slower timeline than the threshold position — β-oxidation enzyme recovery is the typical 5–14 day window, so Day-12 / Day-16 should show further normalization.

CARDIOVASCULAR — STILL ENHANCED

HR at matched watts is still 5–7 bpm below Dec baseline. Plasma volume expansion is durable through Day-8 — Dylan still has the "free" cardiovascular benefit from the ultra.

NEW BASELINE — SmO₂

First test with NIRS data. Quad desats progressively through the test with major demand-supply imbalance at 200 W and ceiling collapse at 275 W. Bicep rebounds at 250 W show good circulatory redistribution. These slopes are now the reference for future tests.

PRACTICAL READ FOR DYLAN

  • Threshold and tempo work is mechanically safe again — VT2 is back, the ceiling has restored.
  • Endurance / Z2 pacing should still be gentle through Day-12. Fat-burning machinery is not fully back, so long efforts will feel more carb-dependent than usual.
  • Subjective check-in: does the "I feel back" point coincide with VT2 recovery (Day-8) or with substrate recovery (likely Day-12)? That's the personal calibration to capture.

WHAT TO WATCH ON DAY-12

  • Fat ox at 200 W — currently 43 g/hr, target ~60 (Dec).
  • RER at 125-175 W — currently 0.87, target ~0.78.
  • CHO ox at 200 W — anomalously sitting at 125 g/hr (close to Day-4 value of 120). Should start coming down.
  • HR trajectory — does it stay low or start drifting up?
  • Quad SmO₂ at 200 W — does the strong desat slope ease?
